title: How I transitioned from RPG Maker to Rosebud and Codex to build my Silkroad-inspired manager game (Demo Available)
author: Double_Car3557
selftext:
Hello everyone,

I have been developing games for a while now. Since I didn't have a strong background in coding, I initially started out using RPG Maker. It was very practical for me—in fact, a game I developed with that engine, *Realm Roads*, is currently available to play for free on Steam.

As AI tools advanced over time, game development became more accessible, and I naturally started incorporating them into my workflow. Inspired by *Silkroad Online*—an MMORPG I loved during my childhood—I wanted to create a 2D management/defense game centered around protecting caravans from thieves. This led to my current project: *Silkroad Defenders: Hunter Manager*.

I initially prototyped and designed the game using **Rosebud AI**, generating the initial draft through specific prompts. For the visuals, I combined RPG Maker’s pre-made assets with AI-generated art from **Getimg.ai**. However, as the project grew and I added more content, the AI environment in Rosebud began to behave a bit erratically. Debugging the complex errors while watching my credits deplete quickly made it hard to justify the cost, though it remains a very successful platform for what it does.

To overcome this, I exported my work and continued development locally using the **Codex Windows application**. Codex allowed me to work much more efficiently. I could create separate topics for different game mechanics and themes, and its direct file-access capabilities allowed for more precise code edits. Plus, the credit usage was far more efficient. For the audio, I generated the music using **Suno AI**, which is the same tool I used for my first game. (And yes, I paid the monthly subscription fees for all these premium AI tools!).

Thanks to this workflow, I have officially released the demo for *Silkroad Defenders: Hunter Manager*. Since it's still a solo-developed project utilizing various AI pipelines, there might still be some bugs or balancing issues.

I would love to get your technical feedback on a few things:

* How do you feel about the transition and workflow between Rosebud and Codex?
* Do the [Getimg.ai](http://Getimg.ai) visuals blend well with the classic RPG Maker assets, or does the art style feel inconsistent?
* Any general bugs or mechanical flaws you notice while playing?
* Is this demo boring ? Maybe need more content, etc.

You can test the demo for free on Steam here:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4949260/Silk\_Road\_Defenders/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4949260/Silk_Road_Defenders/)

Please feel free to criticize my work, my workflow, or the game itself however you wish. I'm eager to learn from this community!
